messages:
jordan: Customer on Dedicated hit repeated tool-call failures when streaming a large payload. tool gets invoked but args are invalid JSON. only happens when client streams ~>10KB in a single call.

liz: rough error from customer? stack/logs?

jordan: error from our side: \"Invalid tool args: unexpected end of JSON input\". They pasted the SSE chunks — one chunk ends with `...\"details\": {\"items\": [1,2` and next chunk starts with `,3]}}`

mike: so chunk boundary split a JSON token. Do we reassemble across SSE events? we should. which component is dropping bytes?

ryan: grabbing wire trace. customer uses a proxy (haproxy) + internal gateway. repro with curl works sometimes. I can attach a minimal repro in a minute.

qa_ana: repro steps I used:
1) small node script that streams a function call body in 8KB chunks to /v1/generate.
2) server returns a toolcall event with args truncated, then error.

qa_ana: example node snippet I used:
```\nconst req = http.request(opts);\nreq.write('event: tool_call\n\ndata: {\"tool\":\"charge\",\"args\":{\"invoice\":\"inv_12345\",\"lines\":[');\nsetTimeout(()=> req.write('1,2,3]}}\n\n'), 20);\nreq.end();\n```

liz: thanks. does our streaming parser assume each SSE `data:` line is a complete JSON blob? we should be tolerant of partial lines.

mike: runtime does `JSON.parse` per SSE `data` chunk currently. that's the bug. we need a streaming JSON reassembler or buffer until balanced braces.

ryan: attaching trimmed tcpdump shows SSE payload bytes: `...5b 31 2c 32` then next packet `2c 33 5d 7d 7d` — so bytes are intact but our proc treats per-packet data as atomic.

jordan: customer noted this only happens behind certain edge proxies which split on MTU boundaries. might be timing/packetization dependent.

liz: short-term mitigation: return 400 with hint to client? doesn't help hosted users. better: change parser to accumulate until a full JSON object is seen (brace/quote-aware).

mike: patch proposal: wrap parser to push incoming SSE data into a small buffer per-request and try incremental parse with a fast bracket counter (skip inside strings). fallback to full parse after N bytes. I can prototype.

deploy-bot: scheduled a canary rollout of parser change to dedicated-canary pool at 2024-06-15T18:00:00Z by mike.

ryan: also found some clients send `data:` lines with `\n` escaped inside which makes naive splitting worse. update tests to include chunked-within-strings cases.

qa_ana: will add a flaky test simulating proxy MTU splits + SSE reassembly.

jordan: customer is ok with ETA for fix, but asked for a reproducible failing trace. I'll send them the tcpdump snippet and the node repro.

liz: thanks team. mike, please post PR link when ready and include perf numbers for incremental parsing vs current.

mike: will do. provisional estimate: small CPU bump on high-req paths but avoids hard failures.

jordan: marked this P1 for support escalation until canary confirms.

ryan: added raw payloads and packet captures to the ticket: https://redwood.zendesk.com/issue/CH-4582

liz: :thumbsup:
